## What I did

Implemented `parallel_letter_frequency::frequency` across the two solution files.

**`parallel_letter_frequency.h`** — declares the API:
```cpp
std::map<char, int> frequency(const std::vector<std::string_view>& texts);
```

**`parallel_letter_frequency.cpp`** — the implementation:
- Splits the list of texts into contiguous chunks and hands each chunk to a worker `std::thread` (count = `std::thread::hardware_concurrency()`, capped at the number of texts).
- Each thread counts letters into its own private 26-element `std::array<int, 26>` (no shared mutable state, so no locks needed).
- After joining all threads, the per-thread arrays are merged into the returned `std::map<char, int>`, inserting only letters whose count is non-zero.
- Uses `std::isalpha`/`std::tolower` on `unsigned char` to count only letters, case-insensitively, and ignore whitespace/punctuation/digits.

## Why this approach

The instructions note that Apple Clang doesn't support the C++17 parallel execution policies, so I used manually-managed `std::thread`s instead. This is portable — it works both locally on Apple Clang and on the Exercism online runner (GCC/`libstdc++`).
